prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1330; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant following a low-speed head-on collision at a residential intersection. Claimant states they were the driver and reports neck and shoulder pain shortly after the impact. Claim file opened and the policyholder confirmed as the named driver on the policy.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant, which confirm the general location and the front-end damage to the vehicle. Damage pattern appears consistent with the impact described in the first report. No independent witnesses have been identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone to go over the account of the collision. Claimant described the sequence of events in the same way as in the initial report. Some uncertainty remains about the claimant's exact seating position in the vehicle at impact, which I have noted for follow-up.

Entry 4: Obtained the repair estimate for the vehicle. Damage shown on the estimate matches the impact the claimant described and the photos on file. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 5: Reviewed the medical records provided by the claimant. The shoulder injury reported is consistent with the type and force of a collision of this kind. No prior injury to the same body area appears in the records or in the claimant's history.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of shoulder injury. I have asked the treating provider for updated notes to confirm the current course of care. Nothing in the file so far suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 7: Reviewed the policy history and confirmed coverage was in force on the date of loss. Claim remains open pending the updated treatment notes and the follow-up on seating position. Next review scheduled once those items are received.
